subject: Re: Kickoff: CATE - M2 status: distillation works, one transfer surprise
body:
Status ahead of the M3 review.

M1 recap: UCF-101 nearest-neighbor repro from the Kinetics-400 checkpoint matched the released demo, and Saoirse's batch API has been embedding internal test libraries since May 20.

M2: Jorge's distillation grid landed its first defensible point - a student at roughly a quarter of the teacher's FLOPs holds within 2.1 points of the teacher on UCF-101 nearest-neighbor top-1, which puts serving cost per embedded minute inside the platform's budget with room to spare. Loss schedule mattered more than architecture; details in his writeup.

The surprise: on the Something-Something v2 checkpoint transfer test, the same recipe loses 6.8 points - temporally-sensitive representations distill much worse than appearance-heavy ones. For M3 this means the endpoint's v1 claim should be scoped to appearance-style similarity (dedup, near-duplicate search) and NOT fine-grained action similarity, or we'll overpromise.

Recommend go, with that scoping. Slides by Jun 26.

Yusuf
